chapters.title: 2 John
body: This short, personal letter opens with real affection — "the elect lady and her children, whom I love in the truth" — and genuine joy that some of them are "walking in truth." The one command John repeats isn't new content, just the same old call to love one another, now urged again because deceivers denying Christ's full humanity have actually begun showing up at people's doors.

"Receive him not into your house" sounds harsh out of context, but it's protective, not merely suspicious — hospitality here risked actively enabling teaching that undermined the very faith being protected. Love and discernment aren't opposites in this letter; welcoming everyone indiscriminately was never what love actually required. John closes wanting to say the rest face to face rather than finish it all on paper — truth and love, for him, were meant to be lived in person, not just written about.
